title: Deficiency Balance Accounts: Returned-Payment Surcharge on Plan Installments
content:
**Rule.** The installment of a new payment plan on an account held under Deficiency Balance Accounts reflects the account's recent bank returns. Two or more returned payments of the account (bank returns of posted deficiency payments, as the account ledger records them) dated fewer than 12 whole months before today carry a surcharge of 8.0 percent, exactly one carries 4.0 percent, and none carries no surcharge. Whole months are counted as the difference in calendar months between the two dates, less one when the later date's day of the month is below the earlier date's.

## Ladder

| Returned payments dated fewer than 12 whole months before today | Surcharge |
|---|---|
| Two or more | 8.0 percent |
| Exactly one | 4.0 percent |
| None | None |

## Points of judgement

- Each return on the ledger counts once, by the date of the return.
- A return dated 12 whole months or more before today is outside the count. Hypothetically, with today the 5th of a month, a return dated the 6th of the same month a year earlier counts, and one dated the 5th of that month a year earlier does not.
- The count is of returns of this account only; a returned payment on the borrower's contract or on another deficiency account is not counted.
- Three returns inside the look-back carry the same 8.0 percent as two.
